resources.title: Lec-16: Introduction to ER model | ER Model kya hai
resources.why_recommended: The clearest exam-focused introduction to entities, attributes and relationships in the ER model, taught in the concise Gate Smashers style that matches GATE expectations.

resources.title: DBMS (Database Management System) Complete Playlist
resources.why_recommended: The most popular end-to-end DBMS course for GATE; its early lectures build the ER model, extended ER features and mapping ER diagrams to relational schemas step by step.

resources.title: Databases: Introduction to Relational Databases (Stanford Online, Jennifer Widom)
resources.why_recommended: Jennifer Widom's canonical Stanford databases course rigorously develops the relational data model and schema design, the theoretical backbone behind ER-to-relational mapping.

resources.title: Lec-51: Projection in Relational Algebra | Database Management System
resources.why_recommended: A short, worked-example lecture on the projection operator that pairs with the selection lecture to cover the core unary relational-algebra operations tested in GATE.

resources.title: Lec-52: Selection in Relational Algebra | Database Management System
resources.why_recommended: Explains the selection operator with clear predicates and examples, the complement to projection for building up relational-algebra query expressions.

resources.title: Database Management Systems (Neso Academy)
resources.why_recommended: Neso Academy's DBMS series gives deep, solved-example coverage of every relational algebra operation (select, project, union, join, division) plus relational calculus, ideal for GATE-level query construction.

resources.title: Databases: Relational Databases and SQL (Stanford Online, Jennifer Widom)
resources.why_recommended: Widom's Stanford course formally develops relational algebra and relational calculus (tuple and domain), giving the precise semantics behind query languages.

topics.topic_name: SQL (DDL/DML/DQL, joins, subqueries, aggregation, GROUP BY/HAVING, views)

resources.title: Lec-79: SQL Aggregate Functions - SUM, AVG(n), COUNT, MIN, MAX Functions | DBMS
resources.why_recommended: Covers the aggregate functions used with GROUP BY/HAVING through concrete examples, one of the most frequently tested SQL areas in GATE.

resources.title: Lec-67: SQL Queries and Subqueries (part-1) | Database Management System
resources.why_recommended: Walks through nested/subquery construction with examples like second-highest salary, exactly the SQL problem style GATE poses.

resources.title: The SQL Language (PostgreSQL 18 Tutorial - Chapter 2)
resources.why_recommended: Official PostgreSQL tutorial covering creating tables, querying, joins, aggregate functions, updates and deletions with runnable examples - authoritative and hands-on.

resources.title: Databases: Relational Databases and SQL (Stanford Online, Jennifer Widom)
resources.why_recommended: Widom's SQL modules cover DDL/DML/DQL, joins, subqueries, aggregation with GROUP BY/HAVING, and views with excellent conceptual clarity and exercises.

resources.title: Concept of Keys in DBMS - Super, Primary, Candidate, Foreign Key, etc
resources.why_recommended: The go-to explainer distinguishing super key, candidate key, primary key, alternate key and foreign key with examples - directly maps to GATE key-identification questions.

resources.title: Types of Keys in Relational Model (Candidate, Super, Primary, Alternate, Foreign)
resources.why_recommended: A concise written reference on all key types plus entity, referential and domain integrity constraints, useful for quick revision before the exam.

resources.title: DBMS (Database Management System) Complete Playlist
resources.why_recommended: The full playlist covers integrity constraints (entity, referential, key, domain) and every key type in sequence, providing complete context around this topic.

resources.title: Lec-33: All Normal Forms with Real life examples | 1NF 2NF 3NF BCNF 4NF 5NF | All in One
resources.why_recommended: A single consolidated lecture taking a schema from 1NF through BCNF (and beyond) with real-life examples - the most efficient way to master normalization for GATE.

resources.title: Databases: Modeling and Theory (Stanford Online, Jennifer Widom)
resources.why_recommended: Widom's design-theory module treats functional dependencies, closure, and normal forms (BCNF, 3NF) with the rigor and decomposition algorithms GATE conceptual questions demand.

resources.title: Normal Forms in DBMS (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF)
resources.why_recommended: A clear written walkthrough of each normal form with dependency-based examples and a comparison table, good for reinforcing the video after watching.

topics.topic_name: Indexing & File Organization (B+ trees, hashing, primary/secondary/clustering index)

resources.title: Lec-111: Primary Index With Example | GATE, PSU and UGC NET | DBMS
resources.why_recommended: Explains the primary (sparse) index with a worked example, the foundation for distinguishing primary, secondary and clustering indexes in GATE numericals.

resources.title: Lec-112: Clustered Index in Database with Example | DBMS
resources.why_recommended: Follows the primary-index lecture to explain clustering indexes on non-key ordering fields with an example, completing the index-type comparison.

resources.title: The Balanced Search Tree (B-Tree) in SQL Databases - Use The Index, Luke!
resources.why_recommended: The definitive vendor-agnostic explanation of how B-tree indexes are structured and searched, including why logarithmic depth keeps lookups fast - deep intuition for the B+ tree topic.

topics.topic_name: Data Types & Data Transformation for Warehousing (min-max/z-score normalization, discretization, sampling, compression)

resources.title: Data Preprocessing in Data Mining (normalization, discretization, reduction)
resources.why_recommended: Covers the full preprocessing pipeline - min-max and z-score normalization, discretization/binning, sampling and data reduction - matching this GATE-DA warehousing sub-topic exactly.

resources.title: Normalization: Min-Max and Z-Score Normalization (Codecademy)
resources.why_recommended: A focused article deriving the min-max and z-score formulas with worked numeric examples - the exact computation GATE asks for on data transformation.

resources.title: NPTEL Data Mining (IIT Kharagpur) - includes data preprocessing and transformation
resources.why_recommended: This IIT Kharagpur NPTEL course covers data preprocessing, normalization, discretization and reduction with the rigor and vocabulary used in the GATE-DA warehousing syllabus.

topics.topic_name: Data Warehouse Modelling & Schemas (star, snowflake, fact constellation, fact/dimension tables, concept hierarchies, measures)

resources.title: Data warehouse schema design - dimensional modeling and star schema
resources.why_recommended: A focused walkthrough of dimensional modeling with fact and dimension tables and the star schema - the core of the data-warehouse modelling sub-topic.

resources.title: Star Schema in Data Warehouse Modeling
resources.why_recommended: Explains star, snowflake and fact-constellation schemas with fact/dimension tables and diagrams, directly covering the modelling terminology GATE-DA lists.

resources.title: Data Warehousing - Schemas (Star, Snowflake, Fact Constellation)
resources.why_recommended: A compact reference contrasting star, snowflake and fact-constellation (galaxy) schemas with example diagrams, good for quick schema comparison.

topics.topic_name: OLAP Operations & OLTP vs OLAP (roll-up, drill-down, slice, dice, pivot)

resources.title: OLAP Operations in DBMS (roll-up, drill-down, slice, dice, pivot)
resources.why_recommended: Defines each OLAP cube operation - roll-up, drill-down, slice, dice, pivot - with concrete cube examples, covering exactly the operations named in the GATE-DA syllabus.

resources.title: What is OLAP? (Online Analytical Processing) - IBM
resources.why_recommended: An authoritative vendor overview contrasting OLAP with OLTP and explaining cube operations, useful for the conceptual OLTP-vs-OLAP comparison GATE asks.

resources.title: NPTEL Data Mining (IIT Kharagpur) - Data Warehousing and OLAP
resources.why_recommended: The IIT Kharagpur data-mining course includes dedicated data-warehousing and OLAP lectures covering the cube model and OLAP operations at GATE depth.
